input.title: SQL injection in public /orders/search via 'customer' query parameter
input.evidence: demo-store-api/app/main.py:15-16 registers GET /orders/search. The docstring at line 17 says the public storefront order lookup page uses it, and the code applies no authentication. Line 18 reads `customer` straight from request.args with no validation. Line 20 puts it into a single-quoted SQL literal with an f-string, and line 21 runs it on a sqlite3 connection (app/db.py:8-11). A request like `?customer=' OR '1'='1` returns every order: id, total and status for all customers. A UNION payload such as `' UNION SELECT name, sql, type FROM sqlite_master--` exposes the schema and other tables. sqlite3's execute() runs only one statement, so stacked queries are blocked, but unauthenticated reading of the whole database still works.
input.recommended_fix: Use a parameterized query: `conn.execute("SELECT id, total, status FROM orders WHERE customer_email = ?", (customer,))`. Also think about whether an unauthenticated lookup by email alone should return order data at all. Requiring an order number plus email, or a logged-in session, would stop people enumerating orders. Add a regression test that sends `' OR '1'='1` and expects zero rows.

input.title: False positive: /reports/status interpolates only allowlisted constant values
input.evidence: demo-store-api/app/main.py:28 reads the user-controlled `status` parameter into `key`. Line 29 maps it through the REPORT_STATUSES dict (lines 8-12), and any unknown key falls back to the constant "OPEN". The value interpolated at line 31 is therefore always one of the hardcoded strings "OPEN", "SHIPPED" or "REFUNDED", never attacker input. Nothing the attacker sends reaches the SQL text. Side note, not part of this finding: the route has no authentication even though its docstring (line 27) calls it an operations dashboard endpoint. It only leaks aggregate counts.
input.recommended_fix: No security fix needed. As defense in depth, and to keep the scanner quiet, switch to a bound parameter: `conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE status = ?", (status,))`. That way a future edit to the allowlist logic can't bring the injection back.

input.title: False positive: f-string SQL in test seed data uses hardcoded constants
input.evidence: demo-store-api/tests/test_search.py:13 builds an INSERT with an f-string. The only interpolated values are the loop index `i` and `email` from the module-level constant SEED_EMAILS (line 7). The seed() helper (lines 10-14) runs only inside the pytest test (lines 17-20), against a temporary database under tmp_path. No HTTP route or production code imports it, and no outside input reaches it.
input.recommended_fix: No security fix needed. Optionally, use `conn.execute("INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?, ?, 10.0, 'OPEN')", (i, email))` so the tests show the safe pattern. You could also exclude tests/ from this rule in the scanner config.

content.text:
I triaged all three scanner findings and saved a draft ticket for each one for human review. One is a real, unauthenticated SQL injection; the other two are false positives.

| ID | Location | Verdict | Severity | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-001 | app/main.py:20 | **Exploitable** | Critical | The `customer` value from the URL (line 18) goes straight into the SQL text (line 20). The route is used by the public order lookup page and has no login check. `' OR '1'='1` returns every order, and a UNION payload can read other tables. |
| F-002 | app/main.py:31 | Not exploitable | None | User input is only used to look up a fixed list of status names (lines 8–12, 29). Only `OPEN`, `SHIPPED` or `REFUNDED` can end up in the query. |
| F-003 | tests/test_search.py:13 | Not exploitable | None | Test-only code. It fills in values from a hardcoded email list (line 7) and writes to a temporary test database. No outside input reaches it. |

**Recommended actions:**
- **F-001:** Fix this one urgently. Pass `customer` as a query parameter (`?` placeholder) instead of putting it into the SQL text, and add a test that tries the injection.
- **Product question for F-001:** Should anyone who knows a customer's email be able to see that customer's orders without logging in?
- **F-002 and F-003:** Switching to `?` placeholders is optional. It would clear the scanner warnings and keep the code safe if it changes later.
- **Side note:** `/reports/status` has no login check, even though it's described as an operations dashboard endpoint. It only exposes order counts per status.
